evidence.excerpt: The average ocean depth is 3,682 meters (12,080 feet).

claims.claim: 挑战者深渊（马里亚纳南端）约 10,935 m（35,876 ft）
used_in: case-02 底部标注与比例注
case-07 海沟底标 + 口径条

evidence.excerpt: Challenger Deep is approximately 10,935 meters (35,876 feet) deep.

claims.claim: 最深点另有常用口径：JetStream 10,994 m；GWR 2020 复核 10,934 m ±3 m

evidence.excerpt: *since updated in 2020 to 10,934 m (35,872 ft) +/- 3 m
…extends from 6,000 meters (19,700 feet) to the very bottom, 10,994 meters (36,070 feet) in the Mariana Trench

claims.claim: HMS Challenger 1875 年首次测得该海沟深度

evidence.excerpt: …whose crew first sounded the depths of the trench in 1875.

claims.claim: 阳光带（epipelagic/sunlight）0–200 m

evidence.excerpt: The upper 200 meters of the ocean is called the euphotic, or "sunlight," zone.
…also called the sunlight zone and extends from the surface to 200 meters (660 feet).

claims.claim: 暮光带（mesopelagic/disphotic）200–1,000 m

evidence.excerpt: …The upper 200 meters of the ocean is called the euphotic…（同页三带结构句）
Mesopelagic Zone: extending from 200 meters (660 feet) to 1,000 meters (3,300 feet)…

claims.claim: 午夜带（bathypelagic/midnight）1,000–4,000 m

evidence.excerpt: The depths from 1,000-4,000 meters (3,300 - 13,100 feet) comprise the bathypelagic zone. Due to its constant darkness, this zone is also called the midnight zone.

claims.claim: 深渊带（abyssopelagic）4,000–6,000 m

evidence.excerpt: The Abyssopelagic Zone (or abyssal zone) extends from 4,000 meters (13,100 feet) to 6,000 meters (19,700 feet).

claims.claim: 超深渊带（hadalpelagic）6,000–11,000 m（带区上界取官方名义值，最深点另见 cl-max 系）
used_in: case-02 带格5（轴画至 10,935 m，名义上界注于口径）

evidence.excerpt: …the hadal zone extends from a depth of 6,000 to 11,000 meters (3.7 to 6.8 miles).
…the hadalpelagic zone extends from 6,000 meters (19,700 feet) to the very bottom, 10,994 meters (36,070 feet) in the Mariana Trench

claims.claim: 『深海』通常从光开始衰减处计起，约 200 m

evidence.excerpt: The deep ocean is generally defined as the depth at which light begins to dwindle, typically around 200 meters (656 feet).

claims.claim: 绝大多数商业渔业与受保护海洋哺乳类/海龟集中在阳光带
used_in: case-01 带格1 tag『多数商业渔业 [S02]』

evidence.excerpt: This zone contains the vast majority of commercial fisheries and is home to many protected marine mammals and sea turtles.

claims.claim: 深海底面积约 3/4 属于深渊带
used_in: case-06 3/4 四格图 + 『软泥与碎屑』卡

evidence.excerpt: Three-quarters of the area of the deep-ocean-floor lies in this zone.

claims.claim: 暮光带开始出现生物发光；鱼眼普遍更大且朝上

evidence.excerpt: …bioluminescence begins to appear on organisms in this zone. The eyes on the fishes are also larger and generally upward directed…

claims.claim: 午夜带水温终年不离约 4 °C（39 °F）

evidence.excerpt: …never fluctuates far from a chilling 39°F (4°C).

claims.claim: 超深渊带由分散的海沟/海槽组成，总面积约澳洲一半

evidence.excerpt: …widely separated ocean trenches and troughs that together occupy an area about half the size of Australia…

claims.claim: 超深渊带以冥王哈迪斯（Hades）得名
used_in: case-01 目录副题『海沟·冥王之界』

evidence.excerpt: Named after Hades, the Greek god of the underworld…

claims.claim: 10 km 深处仍有生物（S21 图片题注）
used_in: case-07 海沟截面内注『10 km 处仍有生物 [S21]』+ 白点示意

evidence.excerpt: Even 10 kilometers (more than 6 miles) down, life finds a way.

claims.claim: 2005 年在挑战者深渊发现生活于其中的有孔虫

evidence.excerpt: In 2005, tiny single-celled organisms called foraminifera… were discovered in the Challenger Deep trench southwest of Guam in the Pacific Ocean.

claims.claim: 最深鱼 Abyssobrotula galatheae 于波多黎各海沟 8,372 m 被记录

evidence.excerpt: The deepest a fish have ever been found, Abyssobrotula galatheae, was in the Puerto Rico Trench at 8,372 meters (27,460 feet).

claims.claim: 光最多可检出至 1,000 m；200 m 之外几乎无有效光照
used_in: case-02 界注『有效光基本止步/光可检出的极限』

evidence.excerpt: Light may be detected as far as 1,000 meters down in the ocean, but there is rarely any significant light beyond 200 meters.

claims.claim: 浮游动物每日垂直移动是『地球上最大的迁徙』，影响气候
used_in: case-04 主件 + 原文引用条

evidence.excerpt: As the greatest migration on Earth, the daily vertical movement of zooplankton in the ocean has a massive influence on sea life and the global climate.

claims.claim: 抹香鲸可下潜至午夜带（1,000–4,000 m）觅食

evidence.excerpt: Yet, sperm whales can dive down to this level in search of food.

claims.claim: 海平面气压 14.7 psi；体内流体外推因此无感
used_in: case-08 规则卡/首行/海面行

evidence.excerpt: At sea level, the air that surrounds us presses down on our bodies at 14.7 pounds per square inch. You don't feel it because the fluids in your body are pushing outward with the same force.

claims.claim: 每下潜 33 ft（10.06 m）压强增加 1 个大气压

evidence.excerpt: For every 33 feet (10.06 meters) you go down, the pressure increases by one atmosphere.

claims.claim: 4,000 m 压强超过 5,850 psi

evidence.excerpt: …at depths of 4,000 meters (13,100 feet), reaches over 5850 pounds per square inch!

claims.claim: Vescovo 引述：舷窗外约 16,000 psi，艇体被压缩近 1/4 英寸

evidence.excerpt: "…you can psychologically feel the 16,000 lb/sq in that's just outside the windows, which is literally compressing the submarine almost a quarter of an inch as you go down." — Victor Vescovo

claims.claim: DEEPSEA CHALLENGER 球壳按全海深当量 16,500 psi（1,138 bar）测试，实测可承 140%

evidence.excerpt: …tested to an equivalent full-ocean-depth pressure of 16,500 pounds per square inch (1,138 bars); strain gauges… indicated that the sphere could withstand up to 140 percent of the test pressure.

evidence.excerpt: "…obtaining soundings with two thousand four hundred and twenty-five fathoms of line…" Sir James Clark Ross … first successful deep-sea sounding ever taken (Jan. 3, 1840).

claims.claim: Marie Tharp（归档原文拼写 Tharpe）在声呐剖面中发现中大洋中脊裂谷（1953）

evidence.excerpt: Marie Tharpe notices a rift valley in sounding profiles along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge…

evidence.excerpt: …Walsh and Piccard logged a depth of 10,912 m (35,800 ft).
